title: A hovered Tree row loses the selection tint it was given
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: Reverting the fix fails the new test with `no hover rule reaches a selected row: expected undefined to be defined`, and it passes with the fix, 10 tests. `npm run ci` exits 0 with every gate run, 631 tests, visual:compare 94/94 at 0 differing pixels. The captures never photograph a hovered row, so the visual gate is silent on this either way, which is why the test asserts the rule rather than a colour.

details:
`components/Tree.md:162` documents selected and hovered together as `background: var(--color-accent-bg-hover)`, a stronger accent than selection alone.

`src/styles/components/tree.css:205` paints the selected row `var(--color-accent-bg)` through a single class. `:353` paints any hovered row `var(--color-row-hover)` through a class and a pseudo-class, which has the higher specificity and wins.

Hovering a selected row therefore replaces the accent tint with plain grey. That is the opposite of what the specification describes.

`--color-accent-bg-hover` is defined at `src/styles/tokens.css:99` and referenced nowhere in `tree.css`.

notes.text: Session agent confirmed every citation in this record against the tree at a374f2c before filing it.

Fixed by giving the hovered selection both classes, so it outranks the general row-hover rule. The same shape applies to a hovered search match, which carries `cs-component-tree-27` and the same resting accent. That was left alone: the specification documents the selected case only, and extending it is a decision rather than a correction.
